record.title: DeepSeek documents public Search and Fetch APIs with per-request billing and account rate limits
record.summary: DeepSeek’s Oct 17 documentation describes raw JSON Search and Fetch APIs for live web content, using the regular API bearer authentication. Search returns structured results from DeepSeek’s in-house engine; Fetch returns one page as Markdown. The guide lists $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests for each API, with 5 requests per second per account for both. It says server-side calls made through Codex, Claude Code or DeepSeek Harness are currently free, with per-request billing scheduled to start Nov 1, 2026, Beijing time. No API call or retrieval-quality evaluation was performed in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DeepSeek’s official documentation presents Search and Fetch as available raw JSON APIs for live web content, using standard API bearer authentication. Search returns structured results from its in-house engine; Fetch returns one page as Markdown.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The published guide lists $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests for each API, independent 5-QPS per-account limits, and says server-side tool calls through Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness are currently free until billing begins at 00:00 Beijing time on 2026-11-01.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No search-quality, coverage, reliability, latency, privacy or safety performance was measured in this review.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent test establishes search coverage, ranking quality, language balance, freshness, extraction fidelity, latency or failure rates.
The inspected guide does not establish query logging/retention, data-use policy, regional processing or detailed safety controls for fetched pages.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as documented, a priced Search and Fetch interface can change the live-web retrieval tools and unit economics available to agent and RAG systems. The consequence is meaningful for integrations, while search quality, coverage, safety and reliability remain unmeasured.
limitations: All access, price, rate-limit and free-period terms are first-party documentation, not independently tested service behavior.
No search quality, source coverage, freshness, page extraction accuracy, latency, uptime or error rate was measured.
The provider’s scale and anti-spam claims in the changelog are not independent evidence of ranking quality.
The guide does not establish query retention, data-use, regional-processing or comprehensive safety controls.
The documented billing transition is future-dated relative to this review and may change.

Search returns structured results from DeepSeek’s in-house engine; Fetch returns one page as Markdown. The guide lists $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests for each API, with 5 requests per second per account for both. It says server-side calls made through Codex, Claude Code or DeepSeek Harness are currently free, with per-request billing scheduled to start Nov 1, 2026, Beijing time. technical.claimed_result: DeepSeek announces Search and Fetch API availability powered by its in-house search engine.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official guide documents endpoint paths, request/response fields, per-successful-request billing and account-level request limits. No runtime behavior was directly tested.
technical.implementation_status: Official docs expose endpoint routes and request schemas. API access eligibility beyond ordinary API authentication, retention, regional coverage and operational service levels were not established.
technical.mechanism: Two JSON endpoints expose live-web retrieval: search accepts query and result controls and returns structured result metadata/content; fetch accepts one URL and returns extracted Markdown. Both use the standard DeepSeek API bearer credential.
technical.novelty: This review does not establish technical novelty relative to other search and fetch APIs.
technical.regime: Documented DeepSeek API access. Search and Fetch each have a 5-QPS per-account cap; Fetch also has per-domain limits. Published per-request billing applies to successful results; server-side calls through named coding assistants are described as free until 2026-11-01 Beijing time.
technical.reproducibility: The contract is publicly documented, but no endpoint request, latency test, retrieval evaluation or bill verification was performed here.
technical.strongest_baseline: No search provider comparison or retrieval-quality baseline is reported in the official guide.

brief.title: DeepSeek documents public Search and Fetch APIs with per-request billing and account rate limits
brief.why_it_matters: A documented live-search and page-fetch interface can expand the tools available to agents and retrieval-augmented applications, with explicit prices and throughput limits that developers can factor into system design. The release establishes a product interface and its announced terms, not search quality, reliability, coverage or safe use.
